# AGENTS.md

Discord Rich Presence for OpenCode V2. Reads OpenCode's local SQLite database
and publishes the project, model, tokens, and cost to Discord.

## Commands

```sh
go test ./...
go vet ./...
go build -trimpath -o bin/opencode-discord-status .
./bin/opencode-discord-status -once
./bin/opencode-discord-status --doctor
./scripts/build.sh          # cross-compile every platform into bin/
```

Go 1.26+ is required.

## Architecture

- `main.go` — flags, poll loop, Discord connection, card text.
- `opencode.go` — SQL, row parsing, busy/idle, session pick, formatting.
- `lifecycle.go` — detect whether OpenCode is running.
- `autostart/index.ts` — OpenCode plugin that starts and stops the watcher.
- `discord/` — minimal Discord IPC client, adapted from `cc-discord-presence`.
- `discord/conn_unix.go` / `conn_windows.go` — platform sockets.

## Invariants

- **Database only.** Read `session_v2` and `session_message` from
  `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`. No plugin and no network access.
- **Busy means** the newest assistant message has no `time.completed`/`finish`, or
  `finish: "tool-calls"`. Any other `finish` is idle.
- **Selection:** busy beats idle, then most recently written. Keep the incumbent
  unless another session is at least 10 seconds newer.
- **Lifecycle:** the `autostart` plugin supervises
  `bin/opencode-discord-status --exit-when-closed`; it starts it with OpenCode
  and kills it on exit. Ignore `opencode-cli serve --service`; it can outlive
  the app. Do not reintroduce a launchd job.
- **Elapsed timer:** start it at the latest user message, not the newest
  assistant step. Assistant messages are per-step, so using them resets the
  timer constantly.
- **Discord IPC state is authoritative.** The client marks itself disconnected
  when the socket closes; `updatePresence` checks `Connected()` before dedupe
  and reconnects, then republishes even if the card text is unchanged.
- **SET_ACTIVITY is request/response.** Nonces are tracked; Discord's `ERROR`
  replies must surface. Do not turn it back into fire-and-forget.
- **Discord rate limits.** Token/cost churn is throttled to one update per four
  seconds; busy/idle and project changes bypass the throttle.
- **Privacy:** only the project folder name, model, tokens, and cost leave the
  machine. Never prompts, messages, or code.
- **Discord client:** keep the IPC framing and the adapted MIT notice in
  `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.

## Setup

Use the `setup-opencode-discord-status` skill in
`.opencode/skills/setup-opencode-discord-status/SKILL.md`, or `SETUP.md`.

# Set up opencode-discord-status

Show OpenCode sessions on Discord: project, model, tokens, and cost. It reads
OpenCode's local SQLite database; there is no plugin and no network.

## Before you start

- Go 1.26+ to build the binary.
- OpenCode V2 and the Discord desktop app on the same machine, signed in.
- No Discord Application ID is needed: the binary ships with a shared one.
  `--client-id` only changes the application name Discord shows.

## Build and run

1. Clone and build:

   ```sh
   git clone https://github.com/Jerit3787/opencode-discord-status.git
   cd opencode-discord-status
   go build -trimpath -o bin/opencode-discord-status .
   ```

2. Run it on the machine with Discord:

   ```sh
   ./bin/opencode-discord-status
   ```

3. Verify:

   ```sh
   ./bin/opencode-discord-status -once
   ./bin/opencode-discord-status --doctor
   ```

   `-once` prints the card without Discord. `--doctor` sets a test card for
   eight seconds.

4. In Discord, enable **User Settings → Activity Privacy → Display current
   activity as a status message**.

## Run only while OpenCode is open

Add the `autostart` plugin to `plugins`:

```jsonc
{
  "package": "/absolute/path/to/opencode-discord-status/autostart",
  "options": {}
}
```

It starts `bin/opencode-discord-status --exit-when-closed` when OpenCode starts,
kills it on exit, and restarts it if it crashes. No launchd job is used. The
app's `opencode-cli serve --service` child is ignored because it can outlive the
app; on macOS, quit with ⌘Q (closing the window is not quitting).

## What it reads

`~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`:

- `session_v2` supplies directory, model, agent, cost, and tokens.
- The newest assistant `session_message` supplies `time.completed` and `finish`.
- Missing `completed`/`finish`, or `finish: "tool-calls"`, means busy.
- Any other `finish` means idle.
- A busy session beats an idle one; the current session is kept unless another
  is clearly newer (10 seconds).

The schema is internal. If a major OpenCode upgrade changes it, update
`opencode.go`.

## Common mistakes

| Mistake | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| Running the binary somewhere without Discord | Run it on the machine with the Discord desktop app. |
| Expecting it to keep running after OpenCode closes | The `autostart` plugin kills it on exit; no launchd job is needed. |
| Using a launchd job at all | Use the `autostart` plugin; it starts and stops with OpenCode. |
| Database path differs | Pass `--db /path/to/opencode.db`. |
| Card is set but invisible | Enable **Display current activity as a status message**. |
| Card stays after quitting on macOS | Closing the window is not quitting; use ⌘Q. The background service is ignored. |

## Verify the result

- `-once` prints a project and a state line.
- `--doctor` shows a test card for eight seconds.
- `--debug` logs each published card; the Discord connection is logged always.
- If nothing appears, check Discord Activity Privacy first.

# opencode-discord-status

[![CI](https://github.com/Jerit3787/opencode-discord-status/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Jerit3787/opencode-discord-status/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

![opencode-discord-status](assets/preview.jpg)

Discord Rich Presence for [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai). Your Discord profile
shows the project you are in, the model doing the work, the token count, and the
session cost.

```
Playing OpenCode
Working on: opencode-discord-status
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash | 12.3K tokens | $0.0421
```

It reads OpenCode's local SQLite database and talks to the Discord desktop app
over its local IPC socket. No plugin, no server connection, no bot token, and no
network traffic.

Full setup: **[SETUP.md](SETUP.md)**. OpenCode agents can load the
`setup-opencode-discord-status` skill in `.opencode/skills/`.

## Quick start

### 1. Build and run

```sh
git clone https://github.com/Jerit3787/opencode-discord-status.git
cd opencode-discord-status
go build -trimpath -o bin/opencode-discord-status .
./bin/opencode-discord-status
```

It ships with a shared Discord application ID, so there is nothing to configure.
OpenCode and Discord must be running on the same machine.

To use your own application name instead, create one at the
[Discord Developer Portal](https://discord.com/developers/applications) and pass
`--client-id`.

### 2. Verify

```sh
./bin/opencode-discord-status -once
```

That prints the card it would publish, without touching Discord:

```
Working on: opencode-discord-status
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash | 12.3K tokens | $0.0421
```

In Discord, enable **User Settings → Activity Privacy → Display current activity
as a status message**.

## Run only while OpenCode is open

Add the `autostart` plugin to the global `plugins` array:

```jsonc
{
  "package": "/absolute/path/to/opencode-discord-status/autostart",
  "options": {}
}
```

OpenCode starts the watcher when it starts and kills it when it exits. There is
no launchd job, and no `opencode-discord-status` process exists while OpenCode
is closed. The plugin checks every two seconds and restarts the watcher if it
crashes.

The watcher is started with `--exit-when-closed`, so it also clears the card and
exits if it is ever orphaned. The desktop app's `opencode-cli serve --service`
child is ignored because it can outlive the app; on macOS, closing the window is
not quitting — use ⌘Q.

To disable it temporarily, set `"options": { "enabled": false }`; set it back to
`true` or remove the option to re-enable.

See [SETUP.md](SETUP.md) for the LaunchAgent.

## What it reads

`~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` (SQLite), from the V2 tables:

| Table | Supplies |
| --- | --- |
| `session_v2` | directory, model, agent, cost, tokens, last update |
| `session_message` | the last assistant message: `time.completed` and `finish` |

Busy and idle:

- no `time.completed` and no `finish` → streaming, **busy**
- `finish: "tool-calls"` → waiting on tools, **busy**
- any other `finish` → **idle**
- no writes for `--idle-after` (default 15 minutes) → **idle**

When several sessions are open, a busy session beats an idle one, then the most
recently written wins. The session already on the card is kept unless another is
clearly newer (10 seconds), so the card does not flicker between two active
projects.

## Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--client-id` | shared app ID | Override with your own Discord Application ID (or `DISCORD_CLIENT_ID`). |
| `--db` | `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` | OpenCode database (`OPENCODE_DB`, then `XDG_DATA_HOME`). |
| `--interval` | `2s` | Poll interval. |
| `--idle-after` | `15m` | Treat a session with no writes for this long as idle. |
| `--exit-when-closed` | `false` | Clear and exit when OpenCode is not running. |
| `--debug` | `false` | Log each published card. |
| `--doctor` | `false` | Set a test card for 8 seconds, then clear it. |
| `--once` | `false` | Print the current card and exit. |

## How it works

- A Go daemon reads the SQLite database with `modernc.org/sqlite` (pure Go, no cgo).
- The last assistant message decides busy/idle; the session row supplies model,
  agent, tokens, and cost.
- A small Discord IPC client performs the `v: 1` handshake and sends
  `SET_ACTIVITY` over the local socket. It reconnects when Discord restarts,
  answers PINGs, and surfaces Discord's errors instead of dropping them.
- Token/cost churn is throttled to one update every four seconds; busy/idle and
  project changes go immediately.
- No plugin entry and no OpenCode restart are needed.

## Development

Requires Go 1.26+.

```sh
go test ./...
go vet ./...
go build -trimpath -o bin/opencode-discord-status .
```

`scripts/build.sh` cross-compiles darwin, linux, and windows binaries into
`bin/`.

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project are documented here. The format follows
[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and this project
adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [1.0.1] - 2026-11-14

### Added

- `options.enabled` switch for the `autostart` plugin, so the presence can be
  disabled without removing the plugin entry.

### Changed

- README and SETUP document the temporary disable flow.

## [1.0.0] - 2026-11-06

First release of the Go, database-backed presence daemon.

### Added

- Standalone Go daemon that reads `session_v2` and `session_message` from
  OpenCode's SQLite database.
- Discord IPC client with handshake validation, PING/PONG, nonce-correlated
  `SET_ACTIVITY`, and automatic reconnect.
- Busy/idle detection from the newest assistant message's `time.completed` and
  `finish`.
- Session picker: busy beats idle, then the most recently written session wins,
  with a 10-second incumbent margin to prevent flicker.
- Card text: `Working on: <project>` over
  `<model> | <tokens> tokens | <cost>`. Idle keeps the project visible.
- Stable elapsed timer based on the latest user message rather than the newest
  assistant step.
- `autostart` plugin that starts and stops the watcher with OpenCode.
- Flags: `--client-id`, `--db`, `--interval`, `--idle-after`,
  `--exit-when-closed`, `--doctor`, `--once`, `--debug`.
- Cross-platform builds for macOS, Linux, and Windows.
- CI matrix on Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows, plus the race detector.
- Setup guide, agent skill, one-command prompt, and preview image.

### Changed

- Defaults to the shared Discord application ID; `--client-id` is only an
  override.
- `{tokens}` is input plus output, formatted like `cc-discord-presence`
  (`12.3K`, `$0.0421`).
- Token/cost churn is throttled to one update every four seconds; busy/idle and
  project changes go immediately.

### Fixed

- Fragmented socket frames are read with `io.ReadFull`.
- Handshake failures (CLOSE/ERROR) and timeouts surface instead of looking
  connected.
- Long-lived clients answer PING and drain `SET_ACTIVITY` replies.
- The client reconnects after Discord restarts even when the card text has not
  changed.
- `SET_ACTIVITY` errors are no longer discarded.
- The elapsed timer no longer resets on every assistant step.
- An orphaned `opencode-cli serve --service` no longer keeps the watcher alive.
- Cost and token formatting edge cases (`$0.00`, `$0.01`, `1.0M`).

### Removed

- The TypeScript plugin and Node watcher.
- The SSH relay and state-file bridge.
- The launchd/LaunchAgent requirement.

## [0.1.0] - 2026-10-24

### Added

- Initial TypeScript plugin for OpenCode V2: project, model, tokens, and cost,
  event-driven updates, a shared per-process Discord connection, and a hub that
  elects one card owner across open projects.

# Setup

This guide is written so a person or an OpenCode agent can follow it top to
bottom. If you are an agent working in this repository, the
`setup-opencode-discord-status` skill in `.opencode/skills/` is the short form.

## Requirements

- OpenCode V2.
- The Discord desktop app, running and signed in, on the same machine as
  OpenCode.
- No Discord Application ID is needed: the binary ships with a shared one. Pass
  `--client-id` only if you want your own application name.
- Go 1.26+ to build the binary.

## Build

```sh
git clone https://github.com/Jerit3787/opencode-discord-status.git
cd opencode-discord-status
go build -trimpath -o bin/opencode-discord-status .
```

`scripts/build.sh` cross-compiles darwin, linux, and windows binaries into
`bin/`.

## Run

```sh
./bin/opencode-discord-status
```

It polls `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` every two seconds and updates the
card when it changes. If Discord restarts, it reconnects and republishes the
current card on the next poll.

`--db` and `OPENCODE_DB` / `XDG_DATA_HOME` control the database path.

## Verify

Print the card without touching Discord:

```sh
./bin/opencode-discord-status -once
```

Expected shape:

```
Working on: opencode-discord-status
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash | 12.3K tokens | $0.0421
```

Then check the Discord path independently:

```sh
./bin/opencode-discord-status --doctor
```

`--doctor` sets a test card for eight seconds and clears it.

Finally, in Discord open **User Settings → Activity Privacy** and enable
**Display current activity as a status message**.

## Run only while OpenCode is open

Add the `autostart` plugin to the global `plugins` array:

```jsonc
{
  "plugins": [
    {
      "package": "/absolute/path/to/opencode-discord-status/autostart",
      "options": {}
    }
  ]
}
```

OpenCode starts `bin/opencode-discord-status --exit-when-closed` when it starts
and kills it when it exits. There is no launchd job and no
`opencode-discord-status` process while OpenCode is closed. The plugin checks
every two seconds and restarts the watcher if it crashes.

The watcher logs to `watch.log` in the repo root.

The desktop app's `opencode-cli serve --service` child is ignored because it can
outlive the app. On macOS, closing the window is not quitting; use ⌘Q.

To disable the presence without removing the entry, set:

```jsonc
"options": { "enabled": false }
```

Set it back to `true` (or remove the option) to turn it on again. OpenCode
reloads the plugin automatically.

## Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--client-id` | shared app ID | Override with your own Discord Application ID. |
| `--db` | `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` | OpenCode database. |
| `--interval` | `2s` | Poll interval. |
| `--idle-after` | `15m` | Treat a session with no writes for this long as idle. |
| `--exit-when-closed` | `false` | Clear and exit when OpenCode is not running. |
| `--debug` | `false` | Log each published card. |
| `--doctor` | `false` | Set a test card for 8 seconds, then clear it. |
| `--once` | `false` | Print the current card and exit. |

## Troubleshooting

**`--once` prints `Idle`** — the database opened but has no current session.

**`--once` prints `Could not read ...`** — the database path is wrong. Pass
`--db`, or set `OPENCODE_DB` / `XDG_DATA_HOME`.

**`Discord not reachable`** — start the Discord desktop app and sign in. The
watcher retries every five seconds.

**Card is set but not visible** — enable **Display current activity as a status
message** in Discord's Activity Privacy settings.

**Card stays after quitting** — the autostart plugin kills the watcher within two
seconds. If it stays, OpenCode is still running: closing the window is not
quitting on macOS; use ⌘Q.

**Discord restarted** — the watcher reconnects on the next poll and republishes
the current card, even if the text has not changed.

**Two projects alternate on the card** — both are working and writing within the
10-second switch margin. The card stays on the current one until the other is
clearly more recent.

**A major OpenCode upgrade changed the database** — the watcher reads
`session_v2` and `session_message`. If those change, update `opencode.go` or
pin the previous binary until the schema settles.

## Upgrading from the TypeScript version

If you used the old plugin, Node watcher, or launchd job:

1. Remove the old `opencode-discord-status` entry from `plugins`. The repo no
   longer contains `index.ts`, so an old entry will fail to load.
2. If you created the old LaunchAgent:
   `launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/dev.opencode.discord-watch` and
   `rm -f ~/Library/LaunchAgents/dev.opencode.discord-watch.plist`.
3. Delete `node_modules` from the clone; it is no longer used.
4. `go build -trimpath -o bin/opencode-discord-status .`
5. Add the `autostart` plugin entry from the section above.

## Uninstall

Remove the `autostart` entry from `plugins`. If you previously installed the
launchd job, also run:

```sh
launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/dev.opencode.discord-watch
rm -f ~/Library/LaunchAgents/dev.opencode.discord-watch.plist
```

Delete the clone if you no longer need it.
